Edinburgh: Scotland's Motorcycle Launch Pad

Edinburgh sits at the junction of Scotland's Lowlands and Highlands, making it an ideal base for motorcycle weekends. Within an hour, you can be riding the empty roads of the Scottish Borders, the Perthshire glens, or the Northumberland moors. Two hours puts you in the heart of the Highlands. Here are five proven weekend routes.

1. Scottish Borders Loop (150 miles)

Head south on the A7 to Selkirk, then take the A708 west to Moffat via St Mary's Loch. Return through the Devil's Beeftub on the A701. This loop covers the Borders' finest roads and can be ridden as a long day or a relaxed overnight. The Moffat House Hotel is an excellent base for the Saturday night.

2. Perthshire and the Trossachs (180 miles)

Cross the Forth Road Bridge and head north through Fife to Perth. From Perth, ride west through the Sma' Glen to Crieff, then south through the Trossachs via the A84. Loch Katrine and the Duke's Pass offer spectacular riding. Return via Stirling and the M9. Add the A85 through Glen Ogle for a Highland bonus.

3. Fife Coastal Route (100 miles)

A gentler option following the Fife coast from the Forth Bridge to St Andrews. The fishing villages of the East Neuk — Elie, Pittenweem, Anstruther, Crail — are charming and the coastal roads offer sea views across the Firth of Forth. St Andrews itself is beautiful, with the ruined cathedral and famous golf courses. Return via the inland A91 through Cupar.

Edinburgh riders have Scotland's entire Central Belt at their feet. The Borders feel like a different world from the city, yet they're only an hour away.

4. Northumberland Cross-Border (160 miles)

Cross the border on the A68 via Carter Bar — one of Britain's most dramatic road crossings with a panoramic viewpoint at the summit. Continue to Hadrian's Wall and ride the Military Road (B6318). Loop back via Kielder Forest or the A696 through Otterburn. This route combines Scottish and English riding in one weekend.

5. The Angus Glens (170 miles)

Head north on the A90 to Forfar, then explore the Angus Glens — Glen Clova, Glen Prosen, and Glen Isla. These deep glacial valleys penetrate the Cairngorm plateau and offer dramatic mountain scenery. The roads end at walking trailheads, giving a genuine sense of adventure. Return via Blairgowrie and the A93 through Perth. Planning Tips

  • Weather: Edinburgh can be dry while the Highlands are wet — check regional forecasts
  • Borders: Best April-October. Quiet year-round compared to the Highlands
  • Fuel: Plentiful in the Borders and Fife. Scarcer in the Angus Glens
  • Accommodation: The Borders has excellent B&Bs at lower prices than the Highlands
keyTakeaways: Edinburgh sits between the Lowlands and Highlands, with the Borders, Perthshire and Northumberland all within an hour.
The Scottish Borders Loop (150 miles) via the A708 past St Mary's Loch and the Devil's Beeftub is quiet year-round.
The Perthshire and Trossachs run (180 miles) takes in the Duke's Pass, Loch Katrine and optionally Glen Ogle.
The A68 crossing at Carter Bar links Scotland and England on the 160-mile Northumberland route.
Borders B&Bs are excellent value compared with Highland accommodation.

comparisonTable.caption: Weekend routes from Edinburgh at a glance

faq.q: Which route is best for quiet roads?
faq.a: The Scottish Borders Loop. Head south on the A7 to Selkirk, take the A708 west to Moffat via St Mary's Loch, and return through the Devil's Beeftub on the A701. This 150-mile loop covers the Borders' finest roads and stays quiet all year compared with the Highlands. The Moffat House Hotel makes an excellent Saturday-night base.

faq.q: Can I reach the Highlands in a weekend?
faq.a: Yes. The Perthshire and Trossachs route (180 miles) delivers genuine Highland scenery without a long slog. Cross the Forth, ride north through Fife to Perth, then west through the Sma' Glen to Crieff and south through the Trossachs on the A84. Loch Katrine and the Duke's Pass are superb; add the A85 through Glen Ogle for a Highland bonus.

faq.q: What is the most scenic border crossing?
faq.a: The A68 over Carter Bar is one of Britain's most dramatic road crossings, with a panoramic viewpoint at the summit. From there, continue to Hadrian's Wall and ride the Military Road, the B6318, before looping back via Kielder Forest or the A696 through Otterburn. This 160-mile route combines Scottish and English riding in a single weekend.

faq.q: Where should I plan fuel stops?
faq.a: Fuel is plentiful across the Borders and Fife, but scarcer in the Angus Glens, where the roads run deep into the Cairngorm plateau and end at walking trailheads. Fill up in Forfar or Blairgowrie before exploring Glen Clova, Glen Prosen and Glen Isla. As always in rural Scotland, top up whenever you pass a station rather than gambling on the next one.

April to October suits all five routes, with the Borders rideable comfortably year-round. Edinburgh can be dry while the Highlands are wet, so check regional forecasts before committing to Perthshire or the Angus Glens. The Borders offer excellent-value B&Bs at lower prices than the Highlands, making an overnight both affordable and worthwhile.
